blueprints.author: 0libote
blueprints.description:
Flexible light control for the IKEA BILRESA scroll wheel remote via Matter.

Created by @0libote
GitHub: https://github.com/0libote/HA-BPs

Setup is top-down: pick the 9 remote event entities, pick the lights for
each preset, then tune the shared wheel and colour feel once.

Each of the three physical BILRESA presets can:
- Control its own set of lights.
- Be disabled.
- Duplicate another preset's lights and colours.
- Share one brightness step, range and transition.
- Share one centre-button layout (Tap = Colour / Hold = Power, or reversed).
- Use its own ordered colour list with Home Assistant's RGB colour picker.
- Reorder colours by dragging them in the blueprint editor.

Presets 2 and 3 duplicate Preset 1 by default, so a single room works after
configuring Preset 1 only. Switch a preset to a custom profile when it
should control different lights or cycle different colours.

Wheel movement uses Matter's totalNumberOfPressesCounted value, so a quick
multi-detent spin is applied as one larger brightness change. Brightness is
clamped to the configured minimum and maximum. Scrolling right while the
preset's lights are off turns them on at the minimum brightness. Tapping
for colour while off turns them on with the first colour.

Updating from an older version resets per-preset tuning to the new shared
Wheel and Colour settings. Re-check those once after updating.

Important Matter limitation:
If the BILRESA itself aborts an over-limit multi-press sequence and sends no
completed event, a blueprint cannot recover that missing movement.

blueprints.docsMarkdown:
## IKEA BILRESA Scroll Wheel
[![Import blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2F0libote%2FHA-BPs%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Fbilresa-scroll-wheel.yaml)

Manual import URL:

```text
https://github.com/0libote/HA-BPs/blob/main/blueprints/bilresa-scroll-wheel.yaml
```

This blueprint turns the three physical BILRESA presets into light profiles
with one shared wheel feel. Each preset keeps its own lights and ordered colour
list, or duplicates another preset. Brightness step, range, transitions and the
centre-button layout are shared so there is far less to tune.

Presets 2 and 3 duplicate Preset 1 by default, so a single room works after
configuring Preset 1 only.

### Before you start

- Pair the BILRESA with Home Assistant through Matter.
- On the device page, identify the three `event` entities for each preset:
  right/brighter, left/dimmer and centre push.
- Confirm that turning or pressing the control updates those event entities.

### Configure

1. Import the blueprint and select **Create automation**.
2. In **Remote buttons**, select the event entities, three per used preset.
   Leave unused slots empty; each slot can accept matching entities from
   multiple remotes. Existing single-entity selections remain supported.
3. In **Lights and presets**, select Preset 1 lights. Keep Presets 2 and 3
   duplicating Preset 1, or switch them to custom lights or disabled.
4. In **Wheel and centre button**, set the shared brightness step, limits,
   transition and tap/hold layout.
5. In **Colours**, order Preset 1 colours. Add custom lists for Presets 2 and
   3 only when they use custom profiles.
6. Save the automation and test tap, hold and both wheel directions.
   **Device Response Wait** bounds acknowledgement between queued gestures;
   increase it if your lights report state slowly.

Scrolling right while a preset's lights are off turns them on at the lower
brightness bound. On/off-only lights are switched on without dimming fields.
Colour while off turns RGB-capable lights on with the first colour; white-only
lights are left alone. Power still controls every available preset light.

Fast wheel movement uses Matter's `totalNumberOfPressesCounted` value, with
the completed `multi_press_N` event type as a fallback when the count attribute
is absent. If the
device itself aborts an over-limit multi-press and publishes no completed event,
Home Assistant has no movement for the blueprint to recover.

Updating from an older version resets per-preset tuning to the new shared
Wheel and Colour settings. Re-check those once after updating.

### Troubleshooting

- No response: watch the selected event entity in **Developer tools > States**
  and confirm it updates when the control is used.
- Wrong direction or button: re-check the three event entities selected for that
  preset.
- Centre button does nothing: check the shared centre-button layout. Tap and
  hold use completed gestures: `multi_press_N` and `long_release` for Matter.
  Initial presses, long-press starts and intermediate multi-press events are ignored.
- Unexpected brightness: check the shared minimum, maximum and per-detent
  step before changing the automation logic.

[View the YAML](https://github.com/0libote/HA-BPs/blob/main/blueprints/bilresa-scroll-wheel.yaml)

blueprint:
  name: IKEA BILRESA Scroll Wheel - 3 Light Presets
  author: 0libote
  description: |
    Flexible light control for the IKEA BILRESA scroll wheel remote via Matter.

    Created by @0libote
    GitHub: https://github.com/0libote/HA-BPs

    Setup is top-down: pick the 9 remote event entities, pick the lights for
    each preset, then tune the shared wheel and colour feel once.

    Each of the three physical BILRESA presets can:
    - Control its own set of lights.
    - Be disabled.
    - Duplicate another preset's lights and colours.
    - Share one brightness step, range and transition.
    - Share one centre-button layout (Tap = Colour / Hold = Power, or reversed).
    - Use its own ordered colour list with Home Assistant's RGB colour picker.
    - Reorder colours by dragging them in the blueprint editor.

    Presets 2 and 3 duplicate Preset 1 by default, so a single room works after
    configuring Preset 1 only. Switch a preset to a custom profile when it
    should control different lights or cycle different colours.

    Wheel movement uses Matter's totalNumberOfPressesCounted value, so a quick
    multi-detent spin is applied as one larger brightness change. Brightness is
    clamped to the configured minimum and maximum. Scrolling right while the
    preset's lights are off turns them on at the minimum brightness. Tapping
    for colour while off turns them on with the first colour.

    Updating from an older version resets per-preset tuning to the new shared
    Wheel and Colour settings. Re-check those once after updating.

    Important Matter limitation:
    If the BILRESA itself aborts an over-limit multi-press sequence and sends no
    completed event, a blueprint cannot recover that missing movement.

  domain: automation
  source_url: https://github.com/0libote/HA-BPs/blob/main/blueprints/bilresa-scroll-wheel.yaml

  homeassistant:
    min_version: 2025.7.0

  input:

    # ============================================================
    # REMOTE
    # ============================================================
    remote:
      name: Remote buttons
      icon: mdi:remote
      collapsed: false
      description: |
        The 9 BILRESA event entities, three per physical preset. On the device
        page, identify right/brighter, left/dimmer and centre push for each
        preset and confirm they update when the control is used.
      input:

        button_1:
          name: Preset 1 - Right / Brighter
          description: Preset 1 scroll-right event entity.
          default: []
          selector:
            entity:
              multiple: true
              filter:
                - domain: event

        button_2:
          name: Preset 1 - Left / Dimmer
          description: Preset 1 scroll-left event entity.
          default: []
          selector:
            entity:
              multiple: true
              filter:
                - domain: event

        button_3:
          name: Preset 1 - Centre Push
          description: Preset 1 centre/push event entity.
          default: []
          selector:
            entity:
              multiple: true
              filter:
                - domain: event

        button_4:
          name: Preset 2 - Right / Brighter
          description: Preset 2 scroll-right event entity.
          default: []
          selector:
            entity:
              multiple: true
              filter:
                - domain: event

        button_5:
          name: Preset 2 - Left / Dimmer
          description: Preset 2 scroll-left event entity.
          default: []
          selector:
            entity:
              multiple: true
              filter:
                - domain: event

        button_6:
          name: Preset 2 - Centre Push
          description: Preset 2 centre/push event entity.
          default: []
          selector:
            entity:
              multiple: true
              filter:
                - domain: event

        button_7:
          name: Preset 3 - Right / Brighter
          description: Preset 3 scroll-right event entity.
          default: []
          selector:
            entity:
              multiple: true
              filter:
                - domain: event

        button_8:
          name: Preset 3 - Left / Dimmer
          description: Preset 3 scroll-left event entity.
          default: []
          selector:
            entity:
              multiple: true
              filter:
                - domain: event

        button_9:
          name: Preset 3 - Centre Push
          description: Preset 3 centre/push event entity.
          default: []
          selector:
            entity:
              multiple: true
              filter:
                - domain: event

    # ============================================================
    # LIGHTS
    # ============================================================
    lights:
      name: Lights and presets
      icon: mdi:lightbulb-group
      collapsed: false
      description: |
        Pick which lights each preset controls. Duplicating reuses that
        preset's lights and colour list. Disabled presets do nothing.
      input:

        preset_1_mode:
          name: Preset 1 Mode
          default: custom
          selector:
            select:
              mode: dropdown
              options:
                - label: Custom profile
                  value: custom
                - label: Disabled
                  value: disabled

        preset_1_lights:
          name: Preset 1 Lights
          description: Lights controlled by this preset. Ignored when disabled.
          default: []
          selector:
            entity:
              multiple: true
              filter:
                - domain: light

        preset_2_mode:
          name: Preset 2 Mode
          default: duplicate_preset_1
          selector:
            select:
              mode: dropdown
              options:
                - label: Duplicate Preset 1 profile
                  value: duplicate_preset_1
                - label: Custom profile
                  value: custom
                - label: Disabled
                  value: disabled

        preset_2_lights:
          name: Preset 2 Lights
          description: Ignored when duplicating Preset 1 or when disabled.
          default: []
          selector:
            entity:
              multiple: true
              filter:
                - domain: light

        preset_3_mode:
          name: Preset 3 Mode
          default: duplicate_preset_1
          selector:
            select:
              mode: dropdown
              options:
                - label: Duplicate Preset 1 profile
                  value: duplicate_preset_1
                - label: Duplicate Preset 2 profile
                  value: duplicate_preset_2
                - label: Custom profile
                  value: custom
                - label: Disabled
                  value: disabled

        preset_3_lights:
          name: Preset 3 Lights
          description: Ignored when duplicating another preset or when disabled.
          default: []
          selector:
            entity:
              multiple: true
              filter:
                - domain: light

    # ============================================================
    # WHEEL AND CENTRE BUTTON (SHARED)
    # ============================================================
    wheel:
      name: Wheel and centre button
      icon: mdi:tune
      collapsed: true
      description: |
        Shared feel for every preset. Scrolling right while the lights are off
        turns them on at the minimum brightness.
      input:

        manual_override:
          name: Manual Override Helpers (Optional)
          description: Turn these helpers ON after a valid remote gesture. Share them with MYGGSPRAY to keep manual lighting until you turn the helpers OFF.
          default: []
          selector:
            entity:
              multiple: true
              filter:
                - domain: input_boolean

        response_timeout:
          name: Device Response Wait
          description: Maximum extra time to wait for each light to acknowledge a command, in addition to its transition. Keeps rapid gestures from reading stale brightness or colour.
          default: 2
          selector:
            number:
              min: 0.1
              max: 10
              step: 0.1
              unit_of_measurement: s
              mode: box

        brightness_step:
          name: Brightness Per Wheel Detent
          description: Percentage changed for each reported wheel detent.
          default: 10
          selector:
            number:
              min: 1
              max: 50
              step: 1
              unit_of_measurement: "%"
              mode: slider

        brightness_min:
          name: Minimum Brightness
          description: Scrolling left will never go below this percentage.
          default: 1
          selector:
            number:
              min: 1
              max: 250
              step: 1
              unit_of_measurement: "%"
              mode: slider

        brightness_max:
          name: Maximum Brightness
          description: Scrolling right will never go above this percentage.
          default: 100
          selector:
            number:
              min: 1
              max: 250
              step: 1
              unit_of_measurement: "%"
              mode: slider

        brightness_transition:
          name: Brightness Transition
          default: 0.2
          selector:
            number:
              min: 0
              max: 5
              step: 0.1
              unit_of_measurement: s
              mode: slider

        centre_layout:
          name: Centre Button Behaviour
          default: tap_colour_hold_power
          selector:
            select:
              mode: dropdown
              options:
                - label: Tap = Colour / Hold = Power
                  value: tap_colour_hold_power
                - label: Tap = Power / Hold = Colour
                  value: tap_power_hold_colour

    # ============================================================
    # COLOURS
    # ============================================================
    colours:
      name: Colours
      icon: mdi:palette
      collapsed: true
      description: |
        Ordered colour lists. Add colours with the RGB colour picker and drag
        rows into the order the centre button should cycle through. The name is
        only for display. Duplicated presets reuse the source preset's list.
      input:

        preset_1_colour_presets:
          name: Preset 1 Colours to Cycle
          default:
            - name: Warm White
              colour: [255, 166, 87]
            - name: Soft White
              colour: [255, 214, 170]
            - name: Daylight
              colour: [255, 244, 229]
            - name: Red
              colour: [255, 0, 0]
            - name: Orange
              colour: [255, 80, 0]
            - name: Yellow
              colour: [255, 220, 0]
            - name: Green
              colour: [0, 255, 0]
            - name: Cyan
              colour: [0, 255, 255]
            - name: Sky Blue
              colour: [0, 170, 255]
            - name: Blue
              colour: [0, 80, 255]
            - name: Purple
              colour: [160, 0, 255]
            - name: Pink
              colour: [255, 0, 120]
            - name: Cool White
              colour: [220, 235, 255]
          selector:
            object:
              multiple: true
              label_field: name
              description_field: colour
              fields:
                name:
                  label: Name
                  required: true
                  selector:
                    text:
                colour:
                  label: Colour
                  required: true
                  selector:
                    color_rgb:

        preset_2_colour_presets:
          name: Preset 2 Colours to Cycle
          description: Ignored when duplicating Preset 1.
          default: []
          selector:
            object:
              multiple: true
              label_field: name
              description_field: colour
              fields:
                name:
                  label: Name
                  required: true
                  selector:
                    text:
                colour:
                  label: Colour
                  required: true
                  selector:
                    color_rgb:

        preset_3_colour_presets:
          name: Preset 3 Colours to Cycle
          description: Ignored when duplicating another preset.
          default: []
          selector:
            object:
              multiple: true
              label_field: name
              description_field: colour
              fields:
                name:
                  label: Name
                  required: true
                  selector:
                    text:
                colour:
                  label: Colour
                  required: true
                  selector:
                    color_rgb:

        colour_transition:
          name: Colour Transition
          default: 0.5
          selector:
            number:
              min: 0
              max: 5
              step: 0.1
              unit_of_measurement: s
              mode: slider


# ==============================================================
# AUTOMATION MODE
# ==============================================================

mode: queued
max: 25
max_exceeded: warning


# ==============================================================
# TRIGGERS
# ==============================================================

triggers:

  # Preset 1
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: !input button_1
    not_to:
      - unknown
      - unavailable
    id: preset1_right

  - trigger: state
    entity_id: !input button_2
    not_to:
      - unknown
      - unavailable
    id: preset1_left

  - trigger: state
    entity_id: !input button_3
    not_to:
      - unknown
      - unavailable
    id: preset1_centre

  # Preset 2
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: !input button_4
    not_to:
      - unknown
      - unavailable
    id: preset2_right

  - trigger: state
    entity_id: !input button_5
    not_to:
      - unknown
      - unavailable
    id: preset2_left

  - trigger: state
    entity_id: !input button_6
    not_to:
      - unknown
      - unavailable
    id: preset2_centre

  # Preset 3
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: !input button_7
    not_to:
      - unknown
      - unavailable
    id: preset3_right

  - trigger: state
    entity_id: !input button_8
    not_to:
      - unknown
      - unavailable
    id: preset3_left

  - trigger: state
    entity_id: !input button_9
    not_to:
      - unknown
      - unavailable
    id: preset3_centre


# ==============================================================
# ACTIONS
# ==============================================================

actions:
  - alias: Require a real device trigger
    condition: template
    value_template: "{{ trigger is defined and trigger.id is defined and trigger.to_state is defined and trigger.to_state is not none }}"


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # RAW INPUT VALUES
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  - variables:

      p1_mode: !input preset_1_mode
      p2_mode: !input preset_2_mode
      p3_mode: !input preset_3_mode

      p1_lights: !input preset_1_lights
      p2_lights: !input preset_2_lights
      p3_lights: !input preset_3_lights

      manual_override: !input manual_override
      response_timeout: !input response_timeout
      brightness_step: !input brightness_step
      brightness_min: !input brightness_min
      brightness_max: !input brightness_max
      brightness_transition: !input brightness_transition
      centre_layout: !input centre_layout

      p1_colour_presets: !input preset_1_colour_presets
      p2_colour_presets: !input preset_2_colour_presets
      p3_colour_presets: !input preset_3_colour_presets
      colour_transition: !input colour_transition

      # Act only on completed gestures. Initial press and long-press start
      # are intermediate events, not independent taps/holds.
      event_type: >-
        {{
          trigger.to_state.attributes.event_type
          if trigger.to_state is not none
          and trigger.to_state.attributes.event_type is defined
          else ''
        }}

      # BILRESA reports a burst of wheel detents in this attribute. Clamped so
      # one spin cannot jump further than intended by an extreme value.
      scroll_clicks: >-
        {% set fallback = event_type.rsplit('_', 1)[-1] | int(1)
                          if event_type.startswith('multi_press_') else 1 %}
        {% set counted = trigger.to_state.attributes.get('totalNumberOfPressesCounted', fallback) %}
        {{ [[counted | int(fallback), 1] | max, 25] | min }}

      legacy_colour_order:
        - warm_white
        - red
        - orange
        - yellow
        - green
        - cyan
        - blue
        - purple
        - pink
        - cool_white

      legacy_colour_map:
        warm_white: [255, 166, 87]
        red: [255, 0, 0]
        orange: [255, 80, 0]
        yellow: [255, 200, 0]
        green: [0, 255, 0]
        cyan: [0, 255, 255]
        blue: [0, 80, 255]
        purple: [160, 0, 255]
        pink: [255, 0, 120]
        cool_white: [220, 235, 255]


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # WHICH PHYSICAL PRESET FIRED, AND WHICH PROFILE DOES IT USE?
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  - variables:

      event_type_lower: "{{ (event_type | string | lower) }}"

      trigger_enabled: >-
        {{
          (
            trigger.id in ['preset1_right', 'preset1_left', 'preset1_centre']
            and p1_mode != 'disabled'
          )
          or
          (
            trigger.id in ['preset2_right', 'preset2_left', 'preset2_centre']
            and p2_mode != 'disabled'
          )
          or
          (
            trigger.id in ['preset3_right', 'preset3_left', 'preset3_centre']
            and p3_mode != 'disabled'
          )
        }}

      source_preset: >-
        {% if trigger.id in ['preset1_right', 'preset1_left', 'preset1_centre'] %}
          1

        {% elif trigger.id in ['preset2_right', 'preset2_left', 'preset2_centre'] %}
          {% if p2_mode == 'duplicate_preset_1' %}
            1
          {% else %}
            2
          {% endif %}

        {% else %}
          {% if p3_mode == 'duplicate_preset_1' %}
            1

          {% elif p3_mode == 'duplicate_preset_2' %}
            {% if p2_mode == 'duplicate_preset_1' %}
              1
            {% else %}
              2
            {% endif %}

          {% else %}
            3
          {% endif %}
        {% endif %}

  - variables:

      # A preset that duplicates a disabled profile must also do nothing.
      # This is a separate step so source_preset from above is already set.
      source_enabled: >-
        {{
          (
            source_preset | int == 1
            and p1_mode != 'disabled'
          )
          or
          (
            source_preset | int == 2
            and p2_mode != 'disabled'
            and p2_mode != 'duplicate_preset_1'
          )
          or
          (
            source_preset | int == 3
            and p3_mode != 'disabled'
          )
        }}


  # Disabled presets stop here.
  - condition: template
    value_template: "{{ trigger_enabled | bool and source_enabled | bool }}"


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # EFFECTIVE PROFILE SETTINGS
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  - variables:

      target_lights: >-
        {{
          p1_lights
          if source_preset | int == 1
          else p2_lights
          if source_preset | int == 2
          else p3_lights
        }}

      chosen_colours: >-
        {{
          p1_colour_presets
          if source_preset | int == 1
          else p2_colour_presets
          if source_preset | int == 2
          else p3_colour_presets
        }}


  - variables:
      target_lights: >-
        {{ expand(target_lights) | selectattr('state', 'in', ['on', 'off'])
           | map(attribute='entity_id') | list }}

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # DERIVED RUNTIME VALUES
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  - variables:

      on_lights: >-
        {{
          expand(target_lights)
          | selectattr('state', 'eq', 'on')
          | map(attribute='entity_id')
          | list
        }}

      # New configurations contain ordered objects:
      #   - name: Red
      #     colour: [255, 0, 0]
      #
      # Older configurations contain a list of preset-name strings. They are
      # normalised here using the old fixed order, preserving old behaviour.
      active_colours: >-
        {% set ns = namespace(items=[]) %}

        {% if chosen_colours | count > 0 and chosen_colours[0] is string %}

          {% for colour_name in legacy_colour_order %}
            {% if colour_name in chosen_colours and colour_name in legacy_colour_map %}
              {% set ns.items = ns.items + [legacy_colour_map[colour_name]] %}
            {% endif %}
          {% endfor %}

        {% else %}

          {% for item in chosen_colours %}
            {% if
              item is mapping
              and item.colour is defined
              and item.colour is sequence
              and item.colour is not string
              and item.colour | count == 3
              and item.colour | select('number') | list | count == 3
              and item.colour | min >= 0
              and item.colour | max <= 255
            %}
              {% set ns.items = ns.items + [item.colour] %}
            {% endif %}
          {% endfor %}

        {% endif %}

        {{ ns.items }}

      centre_action: >-
        {% if event_type_lower in ['long_release', 'hold_release'] %}
          {% if centre_layout == 'tap_power_hold_colour' %}
            colour
          {% else %}
            power
          {% endif %}
        {% elif event_type_lower in ['multi_press_1', 'multi_press_2', 'multi_press_3', 'multi_press_4', 'multi_press_5', 'multi_press_6', 'multi_press_7', 'multi_press_8', 'short_release', 'single_short_release', 'double_short_release', 'single_press', 'double_press', 'single', 'double', 'click', 'tap'] %}
          {% if centre_layout == 'tap_power_hold_colour' %}
            power
          {% else %}
            colour
          {% endif %}
        {% else %}
          ignore
        {% endif %}


  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # STALE MATTER EVENT PROTECTION
  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # The event timestamp must match the state update, not a restored old event.
  # Queued wheel spins can
  # lag a few seconds behind real time, so the window is generous. Without it,
  # an old replayed state after a restart could toggle the lights.
  - condition: template
    value_template: >-
      {{
        trigger.to_state is not none
        and trigger.from_state is not none
        and trigger.from_state.state != trigger.to_state.state
        and as_timestamp(trigger.to_state.state, 0) >= as_timestamp(trigger.to_state.last_changed) - 1
        and not trigger.to_state.attributes.get('restored', false)
        and 0 <= (as_timestamp(now()) - as_timestamp(trigger.to_state.state, 0)) < 30
        and not (event_type_lower == 'short_release' and
          (trigger.to_state.attributes.get('event_types', []) | select('match', '^multi_press_') | list | count > 0))
        and event_type_lower in ['multi_press_1', 'multi_press_2', 'multi_press_3',
            'multi_press_4', 'multi_press_5', 'multi_press_6', 'multi_press_7', 'multi_press_8', 'short_release',
            'single_short_release', 'double_short_release', 'single_press',
            'double_press', 'single', 'double', 'click', 'tap',
            'long_release', 'hold_release']
      }}


  - variables:
      low_brightness: "{{ [brightness_min | float, brightness_max | float] | min }}"
      high_brightness: "{{ [brightness_min | float, brightness_max | float] | max }}"
      dimmable_on_lights: >-
        {% set ns = namespace(lights=[]) %}
        {% for light in expand(on_lights) %}
          {% set modes = light.attributes.get('supported_color_modes', []) %}
          {% if modes and modes != ['onoff'] %}
            {% set ns.lights = ns.lights + [light.entity_id] %}
          {% endif %}
        {% endfor %}
        {{ ns.lights }}
      rgb_lights: >-
        {% set ns = namespace(lights=[]) %}
        {% for light in expand(target_lights) %}
          {% if light.attributes.get('supported_color_modes', [])
                | select('in', ['rgb', 'rgbw', 'rgbww', 'hs', 'xy']) | list | count > 0 %}
            {% set ns.lights = ns.lights + [light.entity_id] %}
          {% endif %}
        {% endfor %}
        {{ ns.lights }}

  - variables:
      rgb_on_lights: >-
        {{ expand(rgb_lights) | selectattr('state', 'eq', 'on') | map(attribute='entity_id') | list }}
      right_targets: "{{ dimmable_on_lights if on_lights | count > 0 else target_lights }}"

  - condition: template
    value_template: >-
      {{ target_lights | count > 0 and
         ((trigger.id.endswith('_right') and right_targets | count > 0 and event_type_lower not in ['long_release', 'hold_release']) or
          (trigger.id.endswith('_left') and dimmable_on_lights | count > 0 and event_type_lower not in ['long_release', 'hold_release']) or
          (trigger.id.endswith('_centre') and
            (centre_action == 'power' or (centre_action == 'colour' and active_colours | count > 0 and rgb_lights | count > 0)))) }}

  - if: "{{ manual_override | count > 0 }}"
    then:
      - action: input_boolean.turn_on
        target:
          entity_id: "{{ manual_override }}"
      - alias: Confirm manual priority before changing lights
        wait_template: >-
          {{ expand(manual_override) | count == manual_override | unique | list | count and
             expand(manual_override) | rejectattr('state', 'eq', 'on') | list | count == 0 }}
        timeout: "{{ [0.001, response_timeout | float(2)] | max }}"
        continue_on_timeout: false

  - choose:
      - alias: Wheel brightness, with device acknowledgement between gestures
        conditions: "{{ trigger.id.endswith('_right') or trigger.id.endswith('_left') }}"
        sequence:
          - repeat:
              for_each: "{{ right_targets if trigger.id.endswith('_right') else dimmable_on_lights }}"
              sequence:
                - variables:
                    can_dim: >-
                      {{ (state_attr(repeat.item, 'supported_color_modes') or []) | count > 0 and
                         state_attr(repeat.item, 'supported_color_modes') != ['onoff'] }}
                    requested_brightness: >-
                      {% if is_state(repeat.item, 'off') %}
                        {{ low_brightness | int }}
                      {% else %}
                        {% set current = state_attr(repeat.item, 'brightness') | int(1) / 255 * 100 %}
                        {% set direction = 1 if trigger.id.endswith('_right') else -1 %}
                        {{ [high_brightness, [low_brightness,
                            current + direction * brightness_step | float * scroll_clicks | int] | max]
                            | min | round(0) | int }}
                      {% endif %}
                - action: light.turn_on
                  continue_on_error: true
                  target:
                    entity_id: "{{ repeat.item }}"
                  data: >-
                    {{ dict(brightness_pct=requested_brightness, transition=brightness_transition)
                       if can_dim else dict() }}
                - wait_template: >-
                    {{ is_state(repeat.item, 'on') and
                       (not can_dim or
                        (state_attr(repeat.item, 'brightness') | float(0) / 255 * 100 - requested_brightness | float) | abs <= 1) }}
                  timeout: "{{ [0.001, brightness_transition | float(0) + response_timeout | float(2)] | max }}"
                  continue_on_timeout: true

      - alias: Centre power with isolated device actions
        conditions: "{{ centre_action == 'power' }}"
        sequence:
          - variables:
              desired_power: "{{ 'off' if on_lights | count > 0 else 'on' }}"
          - repeat:
              for_each: "{{ target_lights }}"
              sequence:
                - action: "{{ 'light.turn_' ~ desired_power }}"
                  continue_on_error: true
                  target:
                    entity_id: "{{ repeat.item }}"
                  data:
                    transition: "{{ brightness_transition }}"
          - wait_template: >-
              {{ expand(target_lights) | selectattr('state', 'eq', desired_power) | list | count == target_lights | count }}
            timeout: "{{ [0.001, brightness_transition | float(0) + response_timeout | float(2)] | max }}"
            continue_on_timeout: true

      - alias: Cycle colours only on lights that support RGB conversion
        conditions: "{{ centre_action == 'colour' }}"
        sequence:
          - variables:
              colour_targets: "{{ rgb_on_lights if rgb_on_lights | count > 0 else rgb_lights }}"
              current_rgb: "{{ state_attr(rgb_on_lights[0], 'rgb_color') if rgb_on_lights | count > 0 else none }}"
          - variables:
              next_rgb: >-
                {% set ns = namespace(best_index=-1, best_distance=999999999) %}
                {% if current_rgb is sequence and current_rgb | count == 3 %}
                  {% for rgb in active_colours %}
                    {% set distance = ((current_rgb[0] | int - rgb[0] | int) ** 2)
                                    + ((current_rgb[1] | int - rgb[1] | int) ** 2)
                                    + ((current_rgb[2] | int - rgb[2] | int) ** 2) %}
                    {% if distance < ns.best_distance %}
                      {% set ns.best_distance = distance %}
                      {% set ns.best_index = loop.index0 %}
                    {% endif %}
                  {% endfor %}
                {% endif %}
                {{ active_colours[(ns.best_index + 1) % (active_colours | count)] }}
          - repeat:
              for_each: "{{ colour_targets }}"
              sequence:
                - action: light.turn_on
                  continue_on_error: true
                  target:
                    entity_id: "{{ repeat.item }}"
                  data:
                    rgb_color: "{{ next_rgb }}"
                    transition: "{{ colour_transition }}"
                - wait_template: >-
                    {% set rgb = state_attr(repeat.item, 'rgb_color') %}
                    {{ is_state(repeat.item, 'on') and rgb is sequence and rgb | count == 3 and
                       (rgb[0] | int - next_rgb[0] | int) | abs <= 20 and
                       (rgb[1] | int - next_rgb[1] | int) | abs <= 20 and
                       (rgb[2] | int - next_rgb[2] | int) | abs <= 20 }}
                  timeout: "{{ [0.001, colour_transition | float(0) + response_timeout | float(2)] | max }}"
                  continue_on_timeout: true

## Doorbell Multi-Speaker TTS Announcement
[![Import blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2F0libote%2FHA-BPs%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Fdoorbell-announcement.yaml)

Manual import URL:

```text
https://github.com/0libote/HA-BPs/blob/main/blueprints/doorbell-announcement.yaml
```

This blueprint announces a press from any selected doorbell binary sensor on
one or more media players. Binary doorbell sensors and doorbell event entities
are supported. The TTS entity, message, announcement volume, bounded playback
wait and fallback volume are configurable. Optional conditions can suppress
announcements, and optional extra actions can add notifications or light effects.

### Configure

1. Import the blueprint and select **Create automation**.
2. Select doorbell binary sensors, doorbell event entities, or both.
3. Select a `tts` entity and the media players that should announce the press.
4. Set the message, announcement volume and maximum playback wait. Previous
   speaker volumes are restored by default; the fallback is used if unavailable.
5. Optionally add conditions or extra actions, then save and test.

The blueprint calls each speaker separately so an error from one speaker does
not prevent the remaining speakers from being attempted. It waits for every
speaker to report new playback, including a fast speaker that has already
finished. If startup is not acknowledged within **Speaker Startup Wait**, it
keeps announcement volume for the full cleanup delay. A volume-only state
update does not count as playback starting. It ignores additional
doorbell presses until the current run, including extra actions, finishes. An available TTS
engine reporting `unknown` before first use is supported. If the engine is
missing or unavailable, speaker volumes are left alone and **Extra Actions**
still run, so notification fallbacks can remain useful. A zero cleanup delay
means almost immediate cleanup; it does not create an unlimited playback wait.

### Troubleshooting

- No announcement: confirm the doorbell entity changes to `on`, and test the
  selected `tts` entity with the speaker in **Developer tools > Actions**.
- Message is cut off: increase **Delay Before Cleanup** and leave **Stop
  Playback After Announcement** disabled. Playback state reporting depends on
  the speaker integration; configure **Speaker Startup Wait** for slow players.
- Wrong volume afterwards: check **Restore Previous Volume** and the fallback
  **Volume After Announcement**. A deliberate volume change during playback is
  left alone. Restoring volume does not generically resume an earlier media session.
- Repeated rings during a run are ignored. A restart/reload interrupts cleanup;
  Home Assistant cannot guarantee volume restoration across that interruption.

[View the YAML](https://github.com/0libote/HA-BPs/blob/main/blueprints/doorbell-announcement.yaml)
blueprints.rawYaml:
blueprint:
  name: Doorbell - Multi-Speaker TTS Announcement
  author: 0libote
  description: |
    Announces a doorbell press on one or more media players.

    Created by @0libote
    GitHub: https://github.com/0libote/HA-BPs

    Behaviour:
    - Starts on a selected binary sensor OFF-to-ON or a fresh doorbell event.
    - Sets every selected speaker to the announcement volume.
    - Speaks the configured message on each speaker through the selected TTS
      entity.
    - After the configured delay, restores each speaker's previous volume
      (or the configured fallback) and optionally stops playback.
    - Supports optional conditions and extra actions.
    - Ignores another press while the current announcement run is active.

  domain: automation
  source_url: https://github.com/0libote/HA-BPs/blob/main/blueprints/doorbell-announcement.yaml

  homeassistant:
    min_version: 2025.7.0

  input:
    doorbell:
      name: Doorbell
      icon: mdi:doorbell
      collapsed: false
      input:
        doorbell_sensors:
          name: Doorbell Sensors
          default: []
          description: Binary sensors that turn on when pressed. Leave empty when using Doorbell Events.
          selector:
            entity:
              multiple: true
              filter:
                - domain: binary_sensor

        doorbell_events:
          name: Doorbell Events (Optional)
          description: Event entities that publish a new timestamp on each ring. Configure sensors, events, or both.
          default: []
          selector:
            entity:
              multiple: true
              filter:
                - domain: event
                  device_class: doorbell

        extra_conditions:
          name: Extra Conditions
          description: Optional conditions such as quiet hours, presence, or house mode.
          default: []
          selector:
            condition:

    announcement:
      name: Announcement
      icon: mdi:account-voice
      collapsed: false
      input:
        tts_entity:
          name: Text-to-Speech Entity
          description: Select the TTS entity that should generate the announcement.
          selector:
            entity:
              filter:
                - domain: tts

        media_players:
          name: Speakers
          description: Select one or more media players for the announcement.
          selector:
            entity:
              multiple: true
              filter:
                - domain: media_player

        message:
          name: Message
          default: Someone is at the door.
          selector:
            text:
              multiline: true

        announcement_volume:
          name: Announcement Volume
          default: 0.6
          selector:
            number:
              min: 0
              max: 1
              step: 0.05
              mode: slider

    cleanup:
      name: After the Announcement
      icon: mdi:volume-minus
      collapsed: false
      input:
        startup_timeout:
          name: Speaker Startup Wait
          description: Maximum time for all available speakers to show new playback. If any speaker does not acknowledge it, keep announcement volume for the full cleanup delay instead of assuming it finished.
          default: 5
          selector:
            number:
              min: 0.1
              max: 30
              step: 0.1
              unit_of_measurement: s
              mode: box

        cleanup_delay:
          name: Delay Before Cleanup
          description: Maximum playback wait after a short startup grace. Cleanup runs earlier when every speaker reports playback finished; increase this for longer messages.
          default:
            hours: 0
            minutes: 0
            seconds: 30
          selector:
            duration:

        restore_previous_volume:
          name: Restore Previous Volume
          description: Restore each speaker's own volume; use Volume After Announcement when disabled or no previous volume is available.
          default: true
          selector:
            boolean:

        normal_volume:
          name: Volume After Announcement
          description: Fallback when no previous volume is known, or fixed volume when Restore Previous Volume is disabled.
          default: 0.3
          selector:
            number:
              min: 0
              max: 1
              step: 0.05
              mode: slider

        stop_after_announcement:
          name: Stop Playback After Announcement
          description: Stop any announcement audio still playing after the cleanup delay.
          default: false
          selector:
            boolean:

        extra_actions:
          name: Extra Actions
          description: Optional actions to run after speaker cleanup, such as a notification or light flash.
          default: []
          selector:
            action:

variables:
  speakers: !input media_players
  restore_volume: !input restore_previous_volume
  announcement_message: !input message
  announcement_level: !input announcement_volume
  normal_level: !input normal_volume
  should_stop: !input stop_after_announcement
  tts_provider: !input tts_entity
  startup_timeout: !input startup_timeout
  playback_timeout: !input cleanup_delay
  playback_seconds: >
    {% if playback_timeout is mapping %}
      {% set duration = timedelta(**playback_timeout) %}
    {% elif playback_timeout is number %}
      {% set duration = timedelta(seconds=playback_timeout) %}
    {% else %}
      {% set duration = as_timedelta(playback_timeout) %}
    {% endif %}
    {{ [0.001, duration.total_seconds() if duration is not none else 30] | max }}

triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: !input doorbell_sensors
    from: "off"
    to: "on"
    id: binary_ring
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: !input doorbell_events
    not_to:
      - unknown
      - unavailable
    id: event_ring

conditions:
  - condition: template
    value_template: >
      {{ trigger.id == 'binary_ring' or
         (trigger.to_state is not none and trigger.from_state is not none and
          trigger.to_state.state != trigger.from_state.state and
          as_timestamp(trigger.to_state.state, 0) >= as_timestamp(trigger.to_state.last_changed) - 1 and
          not trigger.to_state.attributes.get('restored', false) and
          0 <= as_timestamp(now()) - as_timestamp(trigger.to_state.state, 0) < 30) }}

  - condition: and
    conditions: !input extra_conditions

actions:
  - variables:
      available_speakers: >
        {{ expand(speakers) | rejectattr('state', 'in', ['unknown', 'unavailable'])
           | map(attribute='entity_id') | list
           if states[tts_provider] is not none and not is_state(tts_provider, 'unavailable') else [] }}
      playback_timed_out: false
      previous_volumes: >
        {% set ns = namespace(levels={}) %}
        {% for speaker in expand(speakers) %}
          {% if is_number(speaker.attributes.get('volume_level')) and
                0 <= speaker.attributes.volume_level | float <= 1 %}
            {% set ns.levels = dict(ns.levels, **{speaker.entity_id: speaker.attributes.volume_level}) %}
          {% endif %}
        {% endfor %}
        {{ ns.levels }}

  - repeat:
      for_each: "{{ available_speakers }}"
      sequence:
        - if: "{{ is_number(state_attr(repeat.item, 'volume_level')) }}"
          then:
            - action: media_player.volume_set
              continue_on_error: true
              target:
                entity_id: "{{ repeat.item }}"
              data:
                volume_level: "{{ announcement_level }}"

  - variables:
      playback_before: >
        {% set ns = namespace(players={}) %}
        {% for player in available_speakers %}
          {% set speaker = states[player] %}
          {% set ns.players = dict(ns.players, **{player:
            dict(changed=as_timestamp(speaker.last_changed) if speaker is not none else 0,
                 state=speaker.state if speaker is not none else 'unavailable',
                 media=speaker.attributes.get('media_content_id') if speaker is not none else none)}) %}
        {% endfor %}
        {{ ns.players }}

  - repeat:
      for_each: "{{ available_speakers }}"
      sequence:
        - action: tts.speak
          continue_on_error: true
          target:
            entity_id: !input tts_entity
          data:
            cache: true
            media_player_entity_id: "{{ repeat.item }}"
            message: "{{ announcement_message }}"

  - if: "{{ available_speakers | count > 0 }}"
    then:
      - alias: Wait for every speaker to acknowledge new playback or become unavailable
        wait_template: >
          {% set ns = namespace(started=true) %}
          {% for player in available_speakers %}
            {% set speaker = states[player] %}
            {% set previous = playback_before.get(player) %}
            {% if speaker is not none and speaker.state not in ['unknown', 'unavailable'] and
                  previous is not none and
                  as_timestamp(speaker.last_changed) <= previous.changed and
                  speaker.attributes.get('media_content_id') == previous.media %}
              {% set ns.started = false %}
            {% endif %}
          {% endfor %}
          {{ ns.started }}
        timeout: "{{ [0.001, startup_timeout | float(5)] | max }}"
        continue_on_timeout: true
      - variables:
          startup_confirmed: "{{ wait.completed }}"
      - if: "{{ startup_confirmed }}"
        then:
          - alias: Wait for playback completion with a bounded timeout
            wait_template: >
              {{ expand(available_speakers) | selectattr('state', 'in', ['playing', 'buffering']) | list | count == 0 }}
            timeout: "{{ playback_seconds }}"
            continue_on_timeout: true
          - variables:
              playback_timed_out: "{{ not wait.completed }}"
        else:
          - alias: Preserve volume for the full bound when playback was not acknowledged
            delay: "{{ playback_seconds }}"
          - variables:
              playback_timed_out: true

      - repeat:
          for_each: "{{ available_speakers }}"
          sequence:
            - condition: template
              value_template: "{{ states(repeat.item) not in ['unknown', 'unavailable'] }}"
            - if: >
                {{ should_stop and playback_timed_out and
                   states(repeat.item) in ['playing', 'buffering'] and
                   (playback_before[repeat.item].state not in ['playing', 'buffering'] or

Manual import URL:

```text
https://github.com/0libote/HA-BPs/blob/main/blueprints/forgot-to-turn-off.yaml
```

This is a passive safety net for lights controlled manually or by other
automations. It never turns a light on or changes brightness, colour, scenes or
another automation.

### Configure

1. Import the blueprint and select **Create automation**.
2. Select one or more motion, occupancy or presence sensors for the area.
3. Select the lights that may be switched off.
4. Choose how long every sensor must remain clear, then save and test.

The single countdown restarts safely after Home Assistant starts, automations
reload, or a selected light
is turned on while the area is already clear. Unknown or unavailable sensors
are treated as occupied so a sensor fault cannot cause an automatic switch-off.

### Troubleshooting

- Lights remain on: confirm every selected sensor is `off`; unknown or
  unavailable sensors intentionally block switch-off.
- Lights turn off later than expected: activity on any selected sensor cancels
  that countdown, and the full delay starts again once every sensor is clear.
- Test with a short timeout first, then restore the intended safety duration.

  author: 0libote
  description: |

      clear, and turns the selected lights off only if every sensor stays clear
      for the entire configured time.
    - If a selected light is turned on while the area is already clear, starts
      a fresh safety countdown and only acts if all sensors remain clear for
      that entire countdown.
    - If Home Assistant restarts while the area is clear, starts a fresh safety
      countdown rather than immediately switching anything off.
    - Motion or occupancy returning on any selected sensor during a safety
      countdown prevents that countdown from switching the lights off.
    - Unknown or unavailable sensors are treated as not clear, so a sensor fault
      cannot cause an automatic switch-off.

    or replace your existing lighting automations. It is just a final
    "forgot to turn it off" safety net.

  domain: automation
  source_url: https://github.com/0libote/HA-BPs/blob/main/blueprints/forgot-to-turn-off.yaml

  homeassistant:
    min_version: 2025.7.0

  input:
    sensors:
      name: Presence
      icon: mdi:motion-sensor
      collapsed: false
      input:
        presence_sensor:
          name: Motion / Occupancy Sensors
          description: |
            Select one or more sensors covering the area. Every selected sensor
            must stay clear for the full timeout before the lights are switched off.
          selector:
            entity:
              multiple: true
              filter:
                - domain: binary_sensor
                  device_class: occupancy
                - domain: binary_sensor
                  device_class: motion
                - domain: binary_sensor
                  device_class: presence

    lights:
      name: Lighting
      icon: mdi:lightbulb-group-off-outline
      collapsed: false
      input:
        target_lights:
          name: Lights to Turn Off
          description: These lights are only ever switched off by this blueprint.
          selector:
            entity:
              multiple: true
              filter:
                - domain: light

    timing:
      name: Timing
      icon: mdi:timer-outline
      collapsed: false
      input:
        no_presence_duration:
          name: No Presence Before Off
          description: How long every selected sensor must stay continuously clear before the lights are switched off.

variables:
  presence_sensors: !input presence_sensor
  target_lights: !input target_lights

triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id: !input presence_sensor
    to:
    id: presence_changed

  - trigger: state
    entity_id: !input target_lights
    to: "on"
    id: light_turned_on

  - trigger: homeassistant
    event: start
    id: home_assistant_started

  - trigger: event
    event_type: automation_reloaded
    id: automations_reloaded

conditions: []

actions:
  - condition: template
    value_template: >
      {{ trigger is defined and trigger.id is defined and trigger.id in
         ['presence_changed', 'light_turned_on', 'home_assistant_started',
          'automations_reloaded'] }}

  - alias: Only start when every selected presence sensor is clear
    condition: template
    value_template: >
      {{ (presence_sensors | count) > 0
         and (expand(presence_sensors) | list | count) == (presence_sensors | unique | list | count)
         and (expand(presence_sensors)
              | rejectattr('state', 'eq', 'off')
              | list
              | count) == 0 }}

  - alias: Remember exactly when each sensor became clear
    variables:
      clear_state_signature: >
        {% set ns = namespace(parts=[]) %}
        {% for sensor in expand(presence_sensors) | sort(attribute='entity_id') %}
          {% set ns.parts = ns.parts +
             [sensor.entity_id ~ '=' ~ sensor.last_changed] %}
        {% endfor %}
        {{ ns.parts | join('|') }}

  - delay: !input no_presence_duration

  - alias: Every sensor must still be clear
    condition: template
    value_template: >
      {{ (presence_sensors | count) > 0
         and (expand(presence_sensors) | list | count) == (presence_sensors | unique | list | count)
         and (expand(presence_sensors)
              | rejectattr('state', 'eq', 'off')
              | list
              | count) == 0 }}

  - alias: No selected sensor may have detected presence during the countdown
    condition: template
    value_template: >
      {% set ns = namespace(parts=[]) %}
      {% for sensor in expand(presence_sensors) | sort(attribute='entity_id') %}
        {% set ns.parts = ns.parts +
           [sensor.entity_id ~ '=' ~ sensor.last_changed] %}
      {% endfor %}
      {{ ns.parts | join('|') == clear_state_signature }}

  - alias: Only act if at least one selected light is still on
    condition: template
    value_template: >
      {{ (expand(target_lights)
           | selectattr('state', 'eq', 'on')
           | list
           | count) > 0 }}

  - repeat:
      for_each: "{{ expand(target_lights) | selectattr('state', 'eq', 'on') | map(attribute='entity_id') | list }}"
      sequence:
        - alias: Recheck occupancy immediately before each light
          condition: template
          value_template: >
            {% set ns = namespace(parts=[]) %}
            {% for sensor in expand(presence_sensors) | sort(attribute='entity_id') %}
              {% set ns.parts = ns.parts + [sensor.entity_id ~ '=' ~ sensor.last_changed] %}
            {% endfor %}
            {{ expand(presence_sensors) | count == presence_sensors | unique | list | count and
               expand(presence_sensors) | rejectattr('state', 'eq', 'off') | list | count == 0 and
               ns.parts | join('|') == clear_state_signature and is_state(repeat.item, 'on') }}
        - action: light.turn_off
          continue_on_error: true
          target:
            entity_id: "{{ repeat.item }}"

mode: restart
max_exceeded: silent

blueprints.author: 0libote
blueprints.description:
Smart motion lighting for IKEA MYGGSPRAY Matter-over-Thread sensors and
other Home Assistant motion detectors.

Created by @0libote
GitHub: https://github.com/0libote/HA-BPs

Behaviour:
- Starts when any selected motion detector reports motion, at least one
  selected illuminance sensor is below the chosen threshold, and every
  selected light is off and available.
- Motion-only detectors are supported; illuminance can be supplied by
  separate detectors that expose light-level entities.
- Sends brightness and colour in the same light.turn_on call, avoiding an
  intentional "turn on, then dim/recolour" sequence.
- Turns the lights back off after occupancy has stayed continuously clear
  for the configured time.
- Remembers each light's latest normal ON brightness/colour while idle and
  can restore that profile immediately before automatic switch-off.
- Manual/external changes release motion control; OFF always releases it.
- Recovers from stale session locks when all target lights are already off.
- Releases control without darkening the room on sensor/light faults.
- Has a configurable maximum-runtime policy and optional shared manual override.
- Supports extra user-defined activation conditions.

Previous-profile memory:
Home Assistant reports active brightness/colour attributes as null while a
light is off. Without requiring helpers, this blueprint keeps temporary
dynamic scenes whenever target lights are normally ON. Profile tracking is
locked while motion lighting owns the lights, so the automation profile
cannot overwrite the remembered normal profile.

Dynamic scenes are temporary. They are cleared by a Home Assistant restart
or scene reload and are relearned the next time each light is used normally.
If no profile has been learned yet, cleanup still turns the light off but
cannot pre-load its previous brightness/colour first.

Flash prevention:
Home Assistant cannot generically pre-stage brightness/colour while a light
is physically off. This blueprint therefore sends brightness and colour in
one turn_on command. A bulb that itself briefly recalls an old hardware
state before applying that command cannot be fully prevented by a blueprint.

## IKEA MYGGSPRAY Smart Motion Lights
[![Import blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2F0libote%2FHA-BPs%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Fmyggspray-auto-lights.yaml)

Manual import URL:

```text
https://github.com/0libote/HA-BPs/blob/main/blueprints/myggspray-auto-lights.yaml
```

This blueprint starts a motion-lighting session when any selected motion
detector reports activity, at least one selected illuminance sensor says the
room is dark enough, and every selected light is off and available. Motion-only
detectors are supported because the illuminance entities are selected
separately. It can remember the latest normal light profile, restore it before
switch-off and release control after manual changes, unavailable entities or an
overlong session. Faults leave remaining lights on. The default maximum-runtime
policy also leaves lights on; forced OFF is an explicit option.

### Before you start

- Pair the MYGGSPRAY with Home Assistant through Matter-over-Thread.
- Identify the occupancy or motion entities covering the area and at least one
  illuminance entity. They do not have to belong to the same devices.
- Make sure the target lights can be controlled normally from Home Assistant.

### Configure

1. Import the blueprint and select **Create automation**.
2. Select one or more motion/occupancy sensors, one or more illuminance sensors,
   and the target lights.
3. Choose the lux threshold, automation brightness and optional colour.
4. Set the clear delay, maximum session runtime and the runtime-limit policy.
5. Optionally add activation conditions, then save and test in a non-critical
   room first.

The remembered profiles use temporary dynamic scenes. A Home Assistant restart
or scene reload clears them; the blueprint learns them again the next time the
lights are used normally. Restoring an ON profile immediately before OFF may
produce a visible flash on some bulbs; disable profile restoration if that matters.

Active sessions are checked every ten seconds, so switch-off can occur up to ten
seconds after the clear delay. There are no long-lived parallel session timers.
After restart or automation reload the blueprint leaves lights alone and waits
for fresh motion; it does not guess whether an existing ON light was manual.
Activation waits up to five seconds for ON feedback. If it is interrupted or
incomplete, control is released while remaining lights are left alone. A queued
motion event is ignored if the room is already clear when it reaches the queue.

When **Respect Manual Changes** is enabled, a user-context change releases control
immediately. Relevant brightness/colour/effect changes without user context release
control after a ten-second settling period. Physical changes during that period
cannot reliably be distinguished from the bulb applying its automation command.
Use the shared override helper below for deterministic remote priority. A
manual takeover also learns the changed light's new profile from the event,
so restoration does not return it to an older manual setting.

### Troubleshooting

- Motion does not start a session: check the current lux value and confirm every
  target light is both off and available.
- Lights turn off while part of the area is occupied: confirm every selected
  motion detector reports `on` while it detects activity. The clear delay starts
  only after all selected detectors report `off`.
- A previous profile is not restored: use the light normally while the motion
  session is idle so a fresh profile can be learned.
- A bulb briefly flashes an old colour: some bulbs recall their hardware state
  before applying Home Assistant's combined brightness and colour command. A
  generic blueprint cannot pre-stage a physically powered-off bulb.
